checklist: Measured the site boundary and marked the dimensions
Marked north and the direction the site faces
Took photos from every side and from the road
Marked existing trees, plants and water on a plan
Noted the neighbouring buildings and their heights
Noted the road, footpath and entry points
Recorded levels or the direction of slope
Noted the sun path and where shadows fall
Noted the wind direction and sources of noise
Checked local rules: setbacks, height limit, ground coverage

climates.label: Hot and dry
strategies: thick, heavy walls that slow down the heat
small, shaded openings on the sunny sides
a shaded courtyard that cools the air
compact planning so buildings shade each other
water and planting for evaporative cooling

climates.label: Warm and humid
strategies: cross ventilation through thin, open plans
deep roof overhangs and verandahs for shade and rain
raised floors and high ceilings to keep air moving
lightweight walls that do not store heat
shaded outdoor rooms for everyday living

climates.label: Composite (hot summers, monsoon, cool winters)
strategies: a courtyard that works differently in each season
shading that blocks summer sun but lets in winter sun
openable walls for monsoon breezes
thermal mass on the hottest sides
terraces and verandahs as seasonal living spaces

climates.label: Temperate (mild)
strategies: generous openings towards the winter sun
adjustable shading for summer
natural ventilation for most of the year
strong connections between inside and outside
good insulation to keep comfort steady

climates.label: Cold
strategies: a compact form that loses less heat
large openings facing the sun, small ones facing away
thick insulation and airtight construction
entrance lobbies that keep cold air out
sunspaces that collect warmth

drivers.title: Light and shadow
drivers.question: How should daylight feel in the most important space?
moves: Shape the roof to bring light in from above
Use screens or louvres to make patterned shadow
Keep one space deliberately dim to make the next feel bright

drivers.title: Courtyard and void
drivers.question: What happens in the empty space at the heart of the building?
moves: Organise the rooms around one open centre
Carve voids out of a solid block
Link several small courts instead of one large one

drivers.title: Movement and journey
drivers.question: What should a visitor see and feel between the entrance and the main space?
moves: Design a route that reveals the building little by little
Make the stair or ramp the main event
Separate fast routes from slow, wandering ones
diagrams: Sequence of views along the route

drivers.title: Context and street
drivers.question: What does the neighbourhood already do well that the design can continue?
moves: Match the heights and rhythm of the neighbouring buildings
Give something back to the street: a seat, shade, a threshold
Frame one important view of the surroundings

drivers.title: Nature and landscape
drivers.question: Which part of the site is too good to build on?
moves: Keep existing trees and plan around them
Let the ground slope shape the floor levels
Blur the edge between garden and room
diagrams: Site analysis with trees, slope and water

drivers.title: Community and gathering
drivers.question: Where do people meet by accident, and where on purpose?
moves: Place one shared space where all routes cross
Make steps, edges and thresholds wide enough to sit on
Arrange spaces from most public to most private

drivers.title: Material and craft
drivers.question: Which one material tells the story of this place?
moves: Use a local material and show how it is put together
Limit the palette to two or three materials
Let the structure be visible instead of hidden
diagrams: Detail sketch of a key junction

drivers.title: Flexibility and change
drivers.question: How might this building be used differently in ten years?
moves: Use a regular grid that allows rooms to be rearranged
Design one large space that can be divided
Plan for the building to grow in stages
diagrams: Day and night, or now and later, use diagrams
